questions.q: What does the summary say Sam Walton was always willing to do?
a: Copy and improve strategies he saw competitors use
Invent every practice his stores relied on
Avoid looking at what rivals were doing
Buy out competitors before starting himself
questions.why: Lesson 1 says he experimented constantly, borrowing ideas that worked and then making them better or cheaper.

questions.q: Why was Sam once arrested in Brazil?
a: He was measuring aisle widths inside a store
He was photographing a rival's products
He was selling goods without a permit
He was arguing with a store manager
questions.why: Lesson 1 recounts police finding him crawling on a shop floor with a tape measure.

questions.q: What was Sam's single goal for all of his stores?
a: Making every customer as happy as possible
Opening more stores than any rival
Keeping prices higher than local shops
Expanding into foreign markets quickly
questions.why: Lesson 2 says everything he did came back to making each individual customer as happy as he could.

questions.q: What does the summary say about Walmart's profit-sharing plan?
a: It let employees own stock and earn cash bonuses
It was introduced when the company was founded
It applied only to store managers
It was abandoned after a few years
questions.why: Lesson 3 says the plan, started in 1971, gave every employee a share of the company's success through stock and bonuses.

questions.q: What did Walmart employees do when a customer could not find an item?
a: They sent the customer to a local shop that had it
They convinced the customer to buy a substitute
They asked the customer to come back later
They refused to help the customer at all
questions.why: Lesson 2 tells of a paint shop owner who thanked Walmart for sending customers his way.
